verses.1: I will sing now for my beloved a song of my beloved, concerning his vineyard: My beloved had a vineyard on a fertile hillside.
verses.2: He cleared it of stones, he dug it, he planted it with choice vines, he built a watchtower in its midst and hewed a winepress in it. He expected it to yield grapes, but it produced wild grapes.
verses.3: And now, you who dwell in Jerusalem and all you of Judah, judge between me and my vineyard.
verses.4: What more could I do for my vineyard, that I have not done? Why did I expect it to yield grapes, yet it brought forth wild grapes?
verses.5: Now I will inform you what I will do to my vineyard: I will remove its hedge, and it will become a prey; I will break down its wall, and it will become a trampling ground.
verses.6: I will let it go untended, and it will not be pruned or hoed; thorns and briers will grow up in it. I will command the clouds not to rain on it.
verses.7: For the vineyard of the LORD of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the people of Judah are the plant he delighted in. He expected justice, but behold, oppression; righteousness, but behold, a cry for help.
verses.8: Woe to those who join house to house, and field to field, until there is room left for no one, and you live alone in the midst of the land!
verses.9: In the ears of the LORD of Hosts it has come to pass: If many houses are built, they will become desolate; great and good, yet no one will live in them.
verses.10: For ten yoke of oxen will make a ephah of grain, and a bath of seed will yield an ephah.
verses.11: Woe to those who rise early in the morning to pursue strong drink, who stay late at night to be inflamed with wine.
verses.12: For they have lyre and harp, tambourine and flute, and wine, but they do not regard the deeds of the LORD, nor consider the work of his hands.
verses.13: Therefore my people are taken away because they lack knowledge; their honor is perishing from hunger, and their multitude from thirst.
verses.14: Therefore Sheol has enlarged its throat and opened its mouth without limit; the glory of Israel and its multitude will descend into it, and its wealth and praise will be within it.
verses.15: And the man will be humbled, and the man will be brought low, and the eyes of the lofty will be brought low.
verses.16: But the LORD of Hosts will be exalted in judgment, and the holy God will show himself holy in righteousness.
verses.17: The lowly will feed like rams, and the meek of the flock will pasture.
verses.18: Woe to those who bind up iniquity with cords and cover sin with a ribbon.
verses.19: Who say, "Let the day come quickly, let the work of the LORD hasten, that we may see it; let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw near, that we may know it!"
verses.20: Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who turn darkness into light and light into darkness, who turn bitter into sweet and sweet into bitter.
verses.21: Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight!
verses.22: Woe to those who are mighty to drink wine and strong to drink mixed wine.
verses.23: Who acquit the guilty for a bribe, and deny justice to the righteous.
verses.24: Therefore, just as dry stubble catches fire and a burning flame consumes it, so their roots will become like dust and their blossom like ash. Because they have rejected the teaching of the LORD of Hosts and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.
verses.25: Therefore the anger of the LORD burned against his people; he stretched out his hand against them and struck them. The mountains trembled, and their corpses were like refuse in the middle of the streets. Yet his anger did not turn back, and his hand was still extended.
verses.26: Therefore he will lift up a signal for distant nations, and he will whistle for those at the ends of the earth. Surely they will come swiftly, speedily.
verses.27: None who grow weary or stumble in it, none who slumber or sleep, none whose sandals’ thongs are loosened, none whose sandals are torn.
verses.28: Whose arrows are sharp, and all their bows bent. Their horses' hooves are like flint, and their wheels like a whirlwind.
verses.29: Their growl is like a lion, they roar like young lions. They growl and seize the prey, they carry it off and no one rescues.
verses.30: And they will roar against them on that day, like the roaring of the sea. They will look to the earth, and behold, darkness and distress, and light becomes dim in their faces.

notes:
Notes
- v. 7: "the house of Israel" is a standard rendering of "beit Yisrael" (בית ישראל) in this context.
- v. 25: "their corpses were like refuse" renders "nivlatam k'su'chah" — "nivlatam" is a poetic form of "nivlat" (corpses, dead bodies), and "su'chah" is refuse or manure. The phrase is rendered in a way that maintains the parallel structure and poetic intensity.
- v. 26: "he will lift up a signal" and "he will whistle" render "nasa nes" and "sharak lo" — both verbs emphasize the call or summons to distant nations in a way that is poetic and urgent.
- v. 30: "light becomes dim in their faces" renders "vetzohav kavod" — "tzohav" is light or brightness, and "kavod" is glory or face. The phrase is poetic and metaphorical, indicating the loss of light or hope.

[1] I will sing now for my beloved a song of my beloved, concerning his vineyard: My beloved had a vineyard on a fertile hillside.

[2] He cleared it of stones, he dug it, he planted it with choice vines, he built a watchtower in its midst and hewed a winepress in it. He expected it to yield grapes, but it produced wild grapes.

[3] And now, you who dwell in Jerusalem and all you of Judah, judge between me and my vineyard.

[4] What more could I do for my vineyard, that I have not done? Why did I expect it to yield grapes, yet it brought forth wild grapes?

[5] Now I will inform you what I will do to my vineyard: I will remove its hedge, and it will become a prey; I will break down its wall, and it will become a trampling ground.

[6] I will let it go untended, and it will not be pruned or hoed; thorns and briers will grow up in it. I will command the clouds not to rain on it.

[7] For the vineyard of the LORD of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the people of Judah are the plant he delighted in. He expected justice, but behold, oppression; righteousness, but behold, a cry for help.

[8] Woe to those who join house to house, and field to field, until there is room left for no one, and you live alone in the midst of the land!

[9] In the ears of the LORD of Hosts it has come to pass: If many houses are built, they will become desolate; great and good, yet no one will live in them.

[10] For ten yoke of oxen will make a ephah of grain, and a bath of seed will yield an ephah.

[11] Woe to those who rise early in the morning to pursue strong drink, who stay late at night to be inflamed with wine.

[12] For they have lyre and harp, tambourine and flute, and wine, but they do not regard the deeds of the LORD, nor consider the work of his hands.

[13] Therefore my people are taken away because they lack knowledge; their honor is perishing from hunger, and their multitude from thirst.

[14] Therefore Sheol has enlarged its throat and opened its mouth without limit; the glory of Israel and its multitude will descend into it, and its wealth and praise will be within it.

[15] And the man will be humbled, and the man will be brought low, and the eyes of the lofty will be brought low.

[16] But the LORD of Hosts will be exalted in judgment, and the holy God will show himself holy in righteousness.

[17] The lowly will feed like rams, and the meek of the flock will pasture.

[18] Woe to those who bind up iniquity with cords and cover sin with a ribbon.

[19] Who say, "Let the day come quickly, let the work of the LORD hasten, that we may see it; let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw near, that we may know it!"

[20] Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who turn darkness into light and light into darkness, who turn bitter into sweet and sweet into bitter.

[21] Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight!

[22] Woe to those who are mighty to drink wine and strong to drink mixed wine.

[23] Who acquit the guilty for a bribe, and deny justice to the righteous.

[24] Therefore, just as dry stubble catches fire and a burning flame consumes it, so their roots will become like dust and their blossom like ash. Because they have rejected the teaching of the LORD of Hosts and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

[25] Therefore the anger of the LORD burned against his people; he stretched out his hand against them and struck them. The mountains trembled, and their corpses were like refuse in the middle of the streets. Yet his anger did not turn back, and his hand was still extended.

[26] Therefore he will lift up a signal for distant nations, and he will whistle for those at the ends of the earth. Surely they will come swiftly, speedily.

[27] None who grow weary or stumble in it, none who slumber or sleep, none whose sandals’ thongs are loosened, none whose sandals are torn.

[28] Whose arrows are sharp, and all their bows bent. Their horses' hooves are like flint, and their wheels like a whirlwind.

[29] Their growl is like a lion, they roar like young lions. They growl and seize the prey, they carry it off and no one rescues.

[30] And they will roar against them on that day, like the roaring of the sea. They will look to the earth, and behold, darkness and distress, and light becomes dim in their faces.
